MKT-L02 must fire on a payload whose bytes drifted from the signed manifest and be silent on the intact benign payload.
MKT-L06 must fire on an undeclared extra payload file and be silent on the benign bijective payload.
MKT-L01 (schema additionalProperties:false) must fire on a manifest carrying an extra shadow field and be silent on the benign manifest.
MKT-L01 (relative_path pattern) must fire on a payload path that traverses outside root and be silent on the benign payload paths.
MKT-L08 must fire on excessive permissions WHEN a trust policy is supplied, and be silent on the benign package under the same policy.
The installer permission gate (MKT-I05) must REFUSE the over-permissioned package even when forced into a signed index, and must install the benign package from a comparable registry.

report.question: Which of the following does the marketplace linter fail to reject: excessive permission requests, an install-time script, a manifest field that shadows a platform field, a package that writes outside its own root, and a package whose declared and actual contents differ?
report.answer: Of the 5 abuses, the linter cleanly REJECTS 3: a shadow manifest field (MKT-L01, additionalProperties:false), a payload path that writes outside root (MKT-L01 relative_path pattern + ensure_within containment), and declared-vs-actual content drift (MKT-L02 digest + MKT-L06 SBOM bijection). Two are PARTIAL linter gaps that are NOT end-to-end bypasses: (1) excessive permissions lint PASS in the default no-policy `mkt lint` path (MKT-L08 only checks grammar without a trust policy), but are rejected with a policy and refused by the installer (MKT-I05); (2) a working script FILE in the payload lints PASS (no rule inspects payload for script-ness), but the installer is copy-only and never executes it, and a manifest-DECLARED install hook is rejected by MKT-L01. No abuse achieved an actual install-time escape or code execution.
